statement: If as many odd numbers as we please be added together, and their multitude be even, the whole will be even.
heath_proof: For let as many odd numbers as we please, AB, BC, CD, DE, even in multitude, be added together; I say that the whole AE is even. For, since each of the numbers AB, BC, CD, DE is odd, if an unit be subtracted from each, each of the remainders will be even; [VII. Def. 7] so that the sum of them will be even. [IX. 21] But the multitude of the units is also even. Therefore the whole AE is also even. [IX. 21]
ai_proof_text:
9.22
**Statement:** If as many odd numbers as we please be added together, and their multitude be even, the whole will be even.

**Step 1.** Let AB, BC, CD, DE be as many odd numbers as we please, even in multitude, added together so that the whole is AE. I say that AE is even.

**Step 2.** Since each of AB, BC, CD, DE is odd, each differs by a unit from an even number [D7.7]; hence, if a unit be subtracted from each of AB, BC, CD, DE, each of the remainders will be even.

**Step 3.** Therefore the sum of all the remainders, being a sum of even numbers, is even [9.21].

**Step 4.** The units subtracted are as many as the odd numbers AB, BC, CD, DE, and the multitude of these odd numbers is even by hypothesis; therefore the units subtracted are even in multitude, that is, taken together they compose an even number.

**Step 5.** Now the whole AE is made up of the sum of the remainders together with the units subtracted. Thus AE is the sum of two even numbers, namely the sum of the remainders (Step 3) and the number composed of the units (Step 4); therefore AE is even [9.21].

**Step 6.** Therefore, if as many odd numbers as we please be added together, and their multitude be even, the whole is even. Q.E.D.
